---
title: "Method and data"
---

## Sources and provenance

The long-form data with a source and a confidence flag on every row is `data/ai_rd_benchmarks.csv`.
Provenance marks in the table cells: no mark means the number was read from the card itself (or from
the METR report the card cites); **\*** means it was read from the lab's launch post because the
card does not give it; **†** means it was read from a search-result excerpt of a write-up and not
found in any primary document; **‡** means it was recalled from memory and not checked. Almost every
cell was verified against the card on 2026-09-13; the handful still marked † or ‡ are launch-blog
figures (SWE-bench Verified for the Codex models, Terminal-Bench for OpenAI models) that no card
contains. Where a later card re-runs an earlier model and gets a different number, the cell keeps
the model's own card value and the notes column records the re-run. The card-by-card verification
record is `data/notes/ai-rd-benchmarks.md`.

Scores are as the lab reports them and are not comparable across labs: each lab uses its own
scaffold, time budget, attempt count and problem subset, and internal suites are only defined
inside one lab. Conditions that change the number are given in parentheses inside the cell.

## Reading the figures

The figures are built for reading saturation. Every bounded metric is drawn on its full range with
the ceiling as a solid line; a human reference point stated by the card (an expert solution, a
threshold the card expresses in human-hours) is a red dotted line; a rule-out threshold not tied to
human performance is a grey dashed line. A black cross sits on a series' last reported value when
the lab's later cards no longer report it, whether because it was retired as saturated, replaced by
a harder version, or dropped from the determination; the documented reason, where the card gives
one, is in the series file. Card names run along the top of each lab's overview at their dates.

Each lab page has, in order: one overview with all of its bounded evaluations on the same 0 to 100
percent axis, so the order in which benchmarks saturate and get replaced is visible; one overview
of its unbounded metrics (speedups, human-normalized scores above 1, time horizons, lower-is-better
errors) on a log axis of multiples, where a series with a card-stated human reference is divided by
it, so 1x is the reference reached, and a series with no reference (METR's time horizons,
Anthropic's staff-survey uplift) is indexed to its first card and drawn dashed; small multiples with
one panel per evaluation; the benchmark-by-model table; and the list of cards. Ceilings,
directions, reference values and retirement dates are in `data/ai_rd_benchmark_series.csv`.

## Which cards are shown

Only cards on the evaluation frontier are shown. A card that improves on at most a quarter of the
evaluations it shares with earlier cards (given at least three shared) adds no frontier
information and is left out of the figures and tables; each lab page names the cards this removes,
and their rows stay in the CSV. Smaller siblings released alongside a frontier model (Sonnet 4,
Haiku 4.5, the Codex addenda, Gemini Flash-Lite) are flagged in the CSV and also left out.

## Files

| path | what |
|---|---|
| `data/ai_rd_benchmarks.csv` | one row per score: lab, model, card, benchmark, conditions, score, source, confidence |
| `data/ai_rd_benchmark_series.csv` | per-series metadata: ceiling, direction, human reference, threshold, category, retirement |
| `data/notes/ai-rd-benchmarks.md` | collection and verification notes, card by card |
| `src/benchmarks.py` | loading, the frontier rule, tables and every figure |

Source: [github.com/tecunningham/ai-rnd-benchmarks](https://github.com/tecunningham/ai-rnd-benchmarks).
